conventions.convention: A randomized procedure is a parameter-independent probability kernel whose probability-measure sections and measurable event evaluations hold at every data point. No auxiliary random-seed representation is asserted.
Statistics are measurable maps into specified measurable target spaces. An estimator has the same target as its estimand; neither parameter measurability nor estimand measurability is imposed.

Binary actions carry the full power-set sigma-algebra; action 1 means reject and action 0 means do not reject. The test function takes values in Borel [0,1]. Null and alternative hypotheses are not part of the test definition.
Action functionals are nonnegative Borel extended-valued functions; their integrals and the iterated-integral identity may equal positive infinity.

load_bearing.statement: A randomized procedure (or randomized decision rule) is a probability kernel K from the experiment's data measurable space to its measurable action space, with probability sections and measurable action-event evaluations at every data point.

For every nonnegative measurable action function g, h_g(x)=∫g(a)K(x,da) is measurable. For each θ, Q_θ(B)=∫K(x,B)P_θ(dx) is a probability measure, and ∫g dQ_θ=∫h_g dP_θ, with nonnegative extended values allowed.
A statistic with target measurable space (Y,B) is a measurable map from the experiment's data space to (Y,B). If ψ:Θ→Y is an estimand, a statistic with this same target space is an estimator of ψ.
A randomized test is a randomized procedure with binary action space {0,1} carrying its full sigma-algebra, where 1 means reject. Its measurable test function is φ(x)=K(x,{1})∈[0,1].

concerns.concern: The Example says the kernel 'assigns probability one to the statistic value T(x)', and step 2.1 says it 'takes the action T(x) with probability one'. The arbitrary target sigma-algebra need not contain the singleton {T(x)}, so a literal singleton-event probability need not be defined. The displayed Dirac kernel and its proof are correct; clarify the wording using measurable events containing T(x), or an explicit deterministic realization.

seams_checked.note: Experiment and estimand uses preserve arbitrary parameter labels, specified sampling laws and absence of parameter measurability. The estimator definition separately equips the estimand target with a sigma-algebra.

Risk uses parameter-independent probability kernels and nonnegative measurable action sections. Bayes-risk statements separately impose parameter and joint measurability; these are not inferred from the procedure definition.
Ancillarity, completeness, sufficiency and minimal sufficiency use measurable statistics. Standard-Borel and common conditional-kernel assumptions are additional explicit conditions.

Real estimators retain their Borel target and stated moment requirements. The deterministic-procedure lemma constructs a Dirac kernel; Rao–Blackwell uses the action-law integration interface with a supplied common conditional kernel.
Rejection functions are measurable [0,1]-valued maps with 1 meaning reject. A separate lemma constructs their binary kernels. Hypotheses, size and p-value validity are added separately.
Sample means and least-squares estimates use the measurable-data-map definition; Euclidean Borel measurability is supplied separately rather than attributed to the statistic definition.
Each fixed-point KDE evaluation is a real-valued estimator after its measurability lemma. Density versions are specified, and point-target identifiability is explicitly not assumed.
At each time, the measurable threshold indicator is interpreted as a rejection function through the separate binary-kernel construction. Anytime validity is an additional distributional property.

Training statistics and score maps retain specified measurability. The independent uniform tie randomization is explicitly supplied, and the text correctly disclaims a general random-seed representation for arbitrary kernels.
